body:
sessions: don't swallow clicks on header meta pills via session drag

## What changed

The Agents window session header container is `draggable` so a session
row can be reordered via drag-and-drop. Its `dragstart` handler already
excluded the *title-actions* toolbar (Run / Open in VS Code / New Chat /
pin / close) from initiating a drag, but never excluded the *meta row*
toolbar, which hosts the changed-files ("X files"), workspace-folder, and
pull-request pills.

This PR extends that same exclusion to also cover the meta row.

## Why

Native HTML5 drag-start and `click` are mutually exclusive browser
events: any small pointer movement between `mousedown` and `mouseup`
(common with a mouse or trackpad) starts a `dragstart` on the header,
which suppresses the subsequent `click` on the button underneath. Since
the meta row wasn't excluded, clicking the changed-files "X files"
summary would intermittently start a session drag instead of opening
the Changes view — matching the reported "click might work but usually
does nothing" symptom exactly (it only "worked" when the pointer stayed
perfectly still during the click).

## Testing

- Added `sessionHeader.test.ts` with regression tests asserting that a
  `dragstart` originating in the meta row (and the title-actions
  toolbar) is prevented, while one starting elsewhere in the header
  still proceeds. Verified the new meta-row test fails without the fix
  and passes with it.
- `scripts/test.sh --grep "Sessions - SessionHeader"` — 3 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- `npm run hygiene` — clean

Fixes #327373

title: agentHost: let subsessions inherit the parent permission level
body:
<!-- Draft: not yet exercised end-to-end in the UI; see "What is not verified". -->

## Problem

A session an agent creates via the `create_session` server tool always starts at the **default** permission level. If the parent session is running at `Allow All`, there is no way to carry that over — and no way to say "yes, and stop asking me".

## What this adds

A new setting **`chat.subsessions.inheritPermissions`** — `once` (default) / `always` / `never`, `APPLICATION_MACHINE` scope (matching `chat.tools.global.autoApprove`).

Under `once`, when the parent runs at an elevated level, the user is asked before the subsession is created:

> This session runs with "Allow All" permissions. Use "Allow All" for the new session (Summarize the README)?
> - Yes, for this new session.
> - No, use default permissions.
> - Always, don't ask again.
> - Never, don't ask again.

The last two options persist the setting. The `create_session` tool call **blocks** until the question is answered.

---

## The non-obvious design decision (please review this first)

**The prompt is a chat input request (elicitation), not extra buttons on the tool confirmation.**

The first implementation added inheritance options to the existing `create_session` confirmation card. That approach is *unworkable*, and it took a live run to prove it:

- When a session is at `Allow All`, the host puts the **Copilot SDK itself** into permission mode `on` (`copilotAgentSession.ts` `_getSdkPermissionMode`).
- The SDK then approves every tool internally and **never calls back into the host**.
- So `SessionPermissionManager.getAutoApproval` is never reached, and the tool emits `toolCallReady confirmed=not-needed` with no options.

Verified in the AHP log from a real run:

```
chat/toolCallStart
chat/toolCallDelta
chat/toolCallReady   confirmed=not-needed  options=[]
chat/toolCallComplete
```
```
Syncing permission mode: configuredLevel=autoApprove, sdkMode=on
```
…and zero occurrences of `Requesting confirmation for tool call`.

**There is no confirmation card to attach buttons to in exactly the case the feature exists for.** The elicitation blocks the tool regardless of SDK permission mode, so it is a real gate.

> Worth noting: unit tests did **not** catch this. They drive the host layer directly, which sits *below* the SDK short-circuit. The failure was only observable end-to-end.

---

## Safety properties

Each of these is a deliberate constraint, and each has a test:

| Constraint | Why |
|---|---|
| Inheritance only on the `autoApprove` axis | Claude models approvals as `permissionMode`, Codex as `permissionsPreset`; both omit `autoApprove` from their session schema. Seeding it would half-elevate the child (host-level bypass, SDK still default). Gated on the parent's schema actually exposing the key. |
| `always` requires directory containment | `always` is the only path that never asks, and the model chooses the child `workspace` freely. Without this, one prompt injection in an `autoApprove` parent yields an unattended auto-approving session rooted anywhere on disk. The level carries over only into a directory already covered by a parent root. |
| Everything ambiguous fails closed | Cancelled/dismissed question, unresolvable level, unknown provider → no inheritance. |
| No freeform answer | A typed reply cannot express a permission decision; it would be read as "no". `allowFreeformInput: false`. |
| Pending questions resolve on dispose | A cancelled turn must never leave a `create_session` call hanging. |

## Concurrent `create_session` calls

An agent can spawn several sessions in one turn. Stacking one card per session is noisy and ambiguous (you can't tell which session you're approving). Questions are therefore **serialized per chat**:

- the first session is asked about alone, identified by its opening prompt;
- answering `yes`/`no` then asks about all remaining ones **together**, by name;
- answering `always`/`never` settles every session still waiting, with no further questions.

## Data flow

```
chat.subsessions.inheritPermissions        (renderer setting)
  └─ agentHost: { key } declarative mirror  → root config: subsessionPermissionInheritance
        └─ SessionPermissionManager.resolveInheritedApprovalLevel()
              ├─ never                → undefined
              ├─ always               → parent level, iff child dir ⊆ parent roots
              └─ once                 → ChatInputRequested … awaits ChatInputCompleted
                    └─ applyCreateSessionTool → IAgentCreateSessionConfig.config.autoApprove
                          └─ CopilotAgent.resolveSessionConfig (validateOrDefault)
```

`validateOrDefault` iterates only *schema* keys, so a seeded `autoApprove` is silently dropped for Claude/Codex — the failure direction is safe by construction, and the explicit guard means we never *offer* inheritance we can't honor.

## Known gap (deliberate)

Enterprise policy that forbids auto-approval (`chat.tools.global.autoApprove` policy value `false`) is clamped **renderer-side** (`isAutoApprovePolicyRestricted`), so no session can be *newly* elevated under policy. A session that was already elevated *before* the policy applied could still have that level inherited by a subsession.

An earlier revision forwarded a dedicated `elevatedApprovalsRestricted` root key for this. That was dropped when rebasing onto the new declarative settings mirroring (`agentHost: { key }`, #329260), which is strictly one root key per setting and offers no hook for a second, policy-derived key. Closing this properly means registering a policy-backed setting, which carries its own policy-lifecycle process and does not belong in this PR. Flagging it explicitly rather than shipping a workaround.

## Review notes

- `IServerToolGroup.execute` / `executeTool` gained an optional `IServerToolExecutionContext`. It is currently unused by the inheritance path (which resolves per-workspace, not per-tool-call) but is plumbed for Copilot/Codex; **reviewers may reasonably ask whether to drop it** — say the word and I'll revert that hunk.
- `matchesServerToolName` moved from `serverToolGroups.ts` to `serverToolNames.ts` so display and policy share one implementation. Its use is still display-only.
- Codex's `toolCallId` lookup moved above the server-tool dispatch; no behavior change for other tools (it's a non-throwing `?.` read, and the branch returns before the pre-existing client-tool lookup).

## Testing

- **14 new tests** in `sessionPermissions.test.ts` covering the policy matrix, provider gating, containment, and the serialized-question semantics; **2** in `sessionServerTools.test.ts` for config seeding.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, hygiene: clean.
- Full agent-host suite: **1283 passing** (rebased onto `main`).

## What is *not* verified

I have confirmed the host emits the question and honors the answer, and that both root-config keys reach a running agent host (observed in the AHP log). I have **not** driven the flow through the UI to confirm the question renders with the four options and no stray input. That is the main thing to exercise when trying this out.

**To try it:** set a session to `Allow All`, then ask the agent to create a session (e.g. *"create a session in this folder to summarize the README"*).

## Open question for reviewers

Dismissing the question card (**✕**) currently means *don't inherit* — fail-closed, consistent with cancel — and the subsession is still created at default permissions. The alternative is for dismissal to **abort** the `create_session` call entirely. I chose the former; happy to switch.

title: `run_factory` should not accept an unconstrained factory name

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Copilot CLI 1.0.78
- VS Code Version: Code - OSS 1.133.0 (development build)
- OS Version: macOS
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents Window / `run_factory` tool
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: The raw session event stream recorded 13 model-authored `run_factory` calls. Every call failed immediately with `RpcResponseError: No factory registered with name "<name>"`.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Expose `run_factory` to an Agents Window session when no matching factories are registered.
2. Ask the agent to perform a routine single-session task, such as a small rendering refinement or analysis of a local screen recording.
3. Observe that the tool schema accepts any string for `name`, allowing the model to invent plausible names and retry them serially.

In the observed session, the model tried eight implementation-oriented names in roughly 49 seconds:

- `apply_finding`
- `code_implementation_factory`
- `single_task`
- `implementation`
- `code-task`
- `fix-factory`
- `repo_task`
- `review_then_implement`

Later it tried five more invented names for video analysis:

- `video_analysis`
- `analyze_video`
- `single_video_analysis`
- `video-analysis`
- `media_analysis`

These were not host retries: each was a distinct assistant-authored tool call after the preceding runtime rejection. No factory ran.

**Expected**

The tool contract should make invalid factory names impossible or strongly bounded. Prefer dynamically constraining `name` to registered factory names. If no factories are registered, do not expose `run_factory`. If dynamic enum generation is not possible, require registry discovery before invocation and return available names in validation errors. The schema should also make `name` required unless `resumeFromRunId` is supplied.

**Actual**

`name` is an optional free-form string, so the model can confuse tool availability with factory availability and repeatedly guess names. The only feedback arrives after each costly tool round trip.

This happened despite session guidance saying orchestration is for non-trivial multi-workstream tasks and repeated delegation failures should fall back to direct work, so prompt guidance alone is not a sufficient guardrail.

title: Monitor secondary repositories for multi-root Agent Host sessions
body:
Follow-up to #329533.

## Problem

`AgentHostChangesetFileMonitorCoordinator` resolves one effective working directory and attaches the session to that directory's repository root. In a multi-folder session this is the primary repository.

The summary refreshes on subscription, turn completion, turn truncation, and primary Git-state events. A change made only in a secondary repository outside an agent turn does not trigger recomputation.

## Example

1. A two-repository session finishes a turn and reports five changed files.
2. The user edits or commits three files in repository B outside the agent.
3. Repository A does not change, so the primary watcher emits no event.
4. Editor Window and Agents Window consumers continue to show five files.
5. The summary becomes correct only after another turn, subscription, or primary event.

## Desired behavior

- Resolve every effective working directory to a repository root.
- Deduplicate folders belonging to the same repository.
- Attach the session to every retained repository watcher.
- Route a change from any root through the existing branch and summary recomputation.
- Coalesce simultaneous events from several repositories.
- Update membership when roots are materialized, added, removed, or remapped.
- Release all references when subscriptions or sessions are disposed.
- Preserve single-folder and non-Copilot behavior.
- Decide whether the existing 20-target computation cap also limits watchers.

## Potential implementation

- Replace the coordinator's session-to-root mapping with a session-to-roots collection.
- Reuse reference-counted root watchers so shared roots are watched once.
- Use effective working directories for inherited and materialized roots.
- Use existing sequencer/debounce infrastructure for bounded coalescing; do not add arbitrary delays.

## Required tests

- A secondary-root change schedules one branch recomputation.
- Multiple folders in one repository create one watcher.
- Simultaneous multi-root events are coalesced.
- Root removal or remapping releases its watcher.
- Session disposal releases every associated root.
- Single-folder and non-Copilot behavior remains unchanged.
- Refreshed state reaches both window surfaces.

title: agents window: fix sessions list icon/animation
body:
Investigated and fixed the missing Sessions-list progress icon.

### Root cause
The shared animation observer removed a spinner from tracking whenever its virtualized row was temporarily detached. When that row was later reattached, the spinner remained paused at its initial all-transparent frame. Scrolling recycled the row and created a newly tracked spinner, explaining why the icon returned.

A live pre-fix probe reproduced `paused: true` with all 6 dots invisible after reattachment. The patched build now reports `paused: false` with visible animated dots.

### Changes
- Kept temporarily detached animations observed until their owner disposes them in `animationSync.ts`.
- Made session read state reactive in the row renderer in `sessionsList.ts`.
- Restored unread-dot priority over completed-state/PR glyphs in `sessionsListModelService.ts`.
- Added regressions in `animationSync.test.ts` and `sessionsListModelService.test.ts`.
- Updated the Sessions-list specification in `SESSIONS_LIST.md`.

title: Update ESLint to v10 (9.x reached end of life on 2026-08-06)
body:
ESLint v9.x reached end of life on 2026-08-06 and no longer receives fixes: https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/ (see also https://eslint.org/version-support/). The repo currently pins `eslint@^9.36.0`.

Findings from running the v10.8 migration locally (`node build/eslint.ts` passes cleanly on the full repo afterwards):

- `typescript-eslint` / `@typescript-eslint/utils` support ESLint 10 since 8.56, so the current `^8.45.0` only needs a bump.
- `@stylistic/eslint-plugin-ts` v2 is a legacy package: the ts-specific plugin was merged into the unified `@stylistic/eslint-plugin`, whose v5 line supports ESLint 10 (rule ids change from `@stylistic/ts/semi` to `@stylistic/semi`).
- `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` declares ESLint 10 support as of v63.
- `eslint-plugin-import` is still on ESLint ≤9: the latest release (2.32.0, June 2025) relies on `context` APIs removed in v10, but works wrapped with `fixupPluginRules()` from `@eslint/compat` (only `import/no-restricted-paths` is used here).
- `eslint-plugin-header` is unmaintained (last release Feb 2021, already needs the `meta.schema = false` workaround on v9) and also works wrapped with `fixupPluginRules()`.

body:
Fixes #329528

### Problem

Per-turn change lists for **Claude** and **Codex** sessions miss **terminal-tool edits**, but Copilot sessions show them.

The Agent Host computes per-turn changes two ways: an authoritative **git checkpoint diff** (includes terminal-tool edits) and a **DB `file_edits` fallback** (misses them). The git path only runs if a per-session **baseline checkpoint** (`turn/0`) was captured — and `captureBaselineCheckpoint` was only invoked from the Copilot harness. Claude and Codex never captured a baseline, so their per-turn changesets always fell back to the DB path.

### Fix

Mirror the Copilot harness — **identical in every way** — for Claude and Codex:

- Inject `IAgentHostCheckpointService` into each harness (same as Copilot).
- Call `captureBaselineCheckpoint(sessionUri, resolvedWorkingDirectories)` on each harness's **fresh** materialize path, **fire-and-forget** (`.catch`, not awaited).
  - **Claude:** in `_materializeProvisional`, before the materialize event fires.
  - **Codex:** on the fresh first send, after the thread is materialized and before `turn/start`, gated `!firstTurnSent && !needsResume` (placed before the resume block clears `needsResume`, so restored sessions are never given a late baseline).

Copilot is unchanged. **No AHP protocol changes.**

### Behavior (inherited from Copilot, no new decisions)

- **Fresh-only:** captured on first materialize, never on resume — restored/pre-existing sessions are not backfilled.
- **Best-effort:** non-git / workspace-less sessions stay on the DB fallback.
- **Idempotent + correctly ordered:** guaranteed by the shared checkpoint service (skips existing baselines; baseline and turn capture share a per-session sequencer).
- **Multi-root:** unchanged — same primary-folder-only read path Copilot has today (tracked separately).

### Tests

- **Claude** (`claudeAgent.test.ts`): baseline captured on fresh materialize; **not** on resume.
- **Codex** (`codexPrewarmEviction.test.ts`): baseline captured on fresh first send; **not** on subsequent sends.
- Existing Claude/Codex test collections wired with `NULL_CHECKPOINT_SERVICE`.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: pass.
- Node unit suite: 13591 passing, 0 failing (no regressions); 4 new tests green.

title: Add an AgentActivate hook with agent-scoped context when switching custom agents
body:
## Feature request

Add a custom-agent lifecycle hook that fires when the active custom agent
changes within an existing chat session, for example `AgentActivate` or
`AgentChanged`.

## Problem

VS Code supports switching custom agents during an existing chat. A common
workflow is:

1. Use an implementation agent for several prompts.
2. Switch to a documentation agent in the same chat.
3. Use that agent for several documentation-specific prompts.
4. Switch to another agent.

An agent-scoped `SessionStart` hook does not run at step 2 because the chat
session has already started. `UserPromptSubmit` can load the documentation
context, but it reruns the hook for every prompt.

There is currently no deterministic lifecycle point meaning "this custom agent
has just become active."

## Proposed behavior

When the selected custom agent changes:

- Fire an `AgentActivate` or `AgentChanged` hook once.
- Provide fields such as:
  - `session_id`
  - `previous_agent`
  - `active_agent`
  - `activation_source` (`picker`, `handoff`, or `subagent`)
  - `cwd`
  - `timestamp`
- Allow the hook to return `additionalContext`.
- Cache and attach that context while the custom agent remains active.
- Remove or deactivate that context when another agent is selected.
- Fire the hook again if the custom agent is later reactivated.

## Example

When I switch from an implementation agent to a documentation agent, the
documentation agent loads project documentation rules and relevant reference
documents once. That context remains effective for the next several
documentation prompts without rerunning a command on every prompt.

When I switch away from the documentation agent, its scoped context no longer
applies.

## Why existing hooks do not cover this

- `SessionStart` runs only at the beginning of a new chat session.
- `UserPromptSubmit` runs on every prompt.
- `SubagentStart` concerns spawned subagents, not selecting another active
  custom agent in the chat panel.
- Static custom-agent instructions cannot replace deterministic loading of
  dynamic project context.

## Related work

This is similar in lifecycle intent to #303777, which requests an on-load hook
for skills, but this request concerns activation of custom agents within an
existing chat.

# [Codespaces Stable] Todo tool references are inconsistently resolved in custom `.agent.md` agents

## Description

In GitHub Codespaces using the Stable VS Code channel, the native Todo tool can be used from the normal GitHub Copilot Chat panel, but several ways of referencing or requesting the same tool from a custom `.agent.md` agent do not work.

The behaviour appears inconsistent between:

- the normal Copilot Chat panel;
- the `tools:` frontmatter of a custom agent; and
- instructions or tool references written in the body of the custom agent.

The Todo functionality/settings are enabled.

## Observed behaviour

### Working

The primary `todo` tool name works when declared in custom-agent frontmatter:

```yaml
---
tools: [todo]
---
```

Also, entering `#todo` directly in the normal Copilot Chat panel creates a Todo list.

I have not yet tested whether a Todo list created this way follows a user-specified/predefined list exactly or whether Copilot independently derives its own Todo items from the prompt. The confirmed behaviour is only that `#todo` in the normal Chat panel successfully activates/creates the Todo UI.

### Not working in custom-agent frontmatter

The following references have not worked when declared in the `tools:` section of a custom `.agent.md` file:

```yaml
---
tools: [ToDoWrite]
---
```

```yaml
---
tools: [todo/TodoWrite]
---
```

```yaml
---
tools: [todo/manage_todo_list]
---
```

Replacing these with:

```yaml
---
tools: [todo]
---
```

makes the native Todo tool available.

### Not working from the `.agent.md` body

Instructions or references in the body of the custom agent also do not reliably make the Todo tool available or cause it to be used.

Examples that have not worked include instructions referring to:

```text
TodoWrite
```

```text
manage_todo_list
```

and:

```text
#todo
```

For example, an agent body instructing the agent to use `#todo` for a multi-step task does not result in the same Todo behaviour that occurs when `#todo` is entered directly in the normal Copilot Chat panel.

## Why this is confusing

The same underlying Todo capability appears to have multiple visible/runtime names depending on the surface, including names such as:

- `todo`
- `TodoWrite`
- `manage_todo_list`

The normal Chat panel recognises `#todo`, while custom agents appear to require the exact `todo` frontmatter entry and do not consistently resolve the other names or body references.

This makes it difficult to determine:

1. which identifier is canonical for `.agent.md` frontmatter;
2. which identifiers are valid aliases;
3. whether namespaced forms such as `todo/TodoWrite` or `todo/manage_todo_list` are intended to resolve;
4. whether a tool referenced in an `.agent.md` body is supposed to be resolved as an actual tool reference or treated only as natural-language instruction; and
5. why `#todo` works when entered directly in Chat but does not produce equivalent behaviour when included in a custom agent's instructions.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a repository in a browser-based GitHub Codespace using the Stable channel.
2. Ensure the Todo functionality/settings are enabled.
3. Create a custom agent under `.github/agents/`.
4. Test the following `tools:` configurations separately:

   ```yaml
   tools: [todo]
   ```

   ```yaml
   tools: [ToDoWrite]
   ```

   ```yaml
   tools: [todo/TodoWrite]
   ```

   ```yaml
   tools: [todo/manage_todo_list]
   ```

5. Start a new chat for each configuration and give the custom agent a multi-step task where a Todo list would be appropriate.
6. Observe that `tools: [todo]` makes the native Todo tool available, while the other tested forms do not.
7. With `tools: [todo]` available, also test custom-agent body instructions that explicitly ask the agent to use `TodoWrite`, `manage_todo_list`, or `#todo`.
8. Observe that these body references do not reliably cause the native Todo tool to be used.
9. In a normal Copilot Chat session, enter `#todo`.
10. Observe that the Todo list UI is created/activated there.

## Expected behaviour

The Todo tool should have one clearly documented canonical identifier for custom agents, with any supported aliases resolving consistently across:

- `.agent.md` `tools:` frontmatter;
- explicit tool references in `.agent.md` body instructions; and
- the normal Copilot Chat panel.

If some identifiers or syntaxes are intentionally valid only in particular contexts, the editor should make those boundaries clear through documentation, validation, IntelliSense, or diagnostics.

In particular, it should be clear why `#todo` works when entered directly in the Chat panel but does not result in equivalent Todo behaviour when referenced from a custom agent body.

## Actual behaviour

In GitHub Codespaces Stable:

- `tools: [todo]` works;
- `tools: [ToDoWrite]` does not;
- `tools: [todo/TodoWrite]` does not;
- `tools: [todo/manage_todo_list]` does not;
- body instructions referring to `TodoWrite` do not reliably invoke Todo;
- body instructions referring to `manage_todo_list` do not reliably invoke Todo;
- body instructions referring to `#todo` do not reliably invoke Todo; and
- `#todo` entered directly in the normal Copilot Chat panel does create/activate a Todo list.

## Environment

- Product: GitHub Codespaces
- Client: VS Code for the Web
- Channel: Stable, not Insiders
- VS Code version: 1.132.0
- Codespace remote OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
- Agent location: `.github/agents/*.agent.md`
- Todo functionality/settings: enabled

## Test scope

This behaviour has only been tested in GitHub Codespaces Stable.

I have not tested:

- VS Code Desktop;
- VS Code Insiders;
- whether Chat-panel `#todo` exactly follows a user-provided/predefined Todo list versus generating its own items.

title: Fix(notebook edit): Fix edit_notebook_file silently failing and repeated "file already exists" errors
body:
Fixes #327473

## Problem

The built-in Copilot agent tool `edit_notebook_file` often reports success but applies no changes when editing an **existing** notebook, while creating a brand-new notebook works fine. Two distinct root causes sit behind this behavior:

### 1. `_createModifiedFileEntry` misclassifies failures and produces repeated "file already exists" errors

In `ChatEditingSession._createModifiedFileEntry`, the `catch` block assumes any failure from `doCreate(ChatEditKind.Modified)` means the file does not exist, then falls back to creating it via `bulkEditService.apply({ edits: [{ newResource: resource }] })` — **without** `overwrite: true`. When the file *does* exist (e.g. the original failure was a notebook model resolution error over SSH Remote), this throws `FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE`, which repeats on every streaming chunk iteration (roughly every ~10 s), flooding the chat output and logs.

### Bug 2: Stale cell IDs produce non-actionable errors

When the model obtains cell IDs via `copilot_getNotebookSummary`, then the notebook is modified before `edit_notebook_file` is invoked, the old cell IDs are stale and no longer present in the cell-ID map. The tool correctly rejects the request, but the error message does not include the currently valid cell IDs, forcing the model to take an extra tool call before it can self-correct.

## Fix

### `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingSession.ts`
- Before the create-fallback in the catch block, check `await this._fileService.exists(notebookUri)`.
  - If the file already exists, **rethrow the original error** instead of assuming the file needs to be created — this stops the repeated `FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE` "file already exists" loop.
  - Only run the create-fallback when the file genuinely does not exist.

### `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/editNotebookTool.tsx`
- `getInvalidCellErrorMessage` now accepts an optional `NotebookDocument` parameter. When a notebook is supplied, the error message includes the list of currently valid cell IDs, so the model can retry immediately with a correct ID instead of doing an extra tool call.

## Impact

- Fixes the confusing silent no-op (success reported, notebook unchanged) that erodes trust in the built-in agent tool.
- Stops the repeated error spam that appears roughly every 10 seconds in streaming sessions.
- Reduces agent tool calls and latency by handing the model the exact valid cell IDs on the first rejection.

## Known limitations

- The valid cell-ID list is best-effort; if the notebook document is unavailable, the error falls back to the previous message (no ID list is shown).
- If the notebook is modified concurrently between reading the summary and the check, a subsequent retry may still race until the model refreshs its understanding.
- The exists-check is a guard on the error path only; it does not change the normal create flow.

- v1 (this PR): initial fix for both root cause (a) and root cause (b).

title: editor: avoid telemetry creation after disposal
body:
## Why

A recent Code Insiders renderer log captured an inline-completions request settling after its editor-scoped instantiation service had already been disposed:

```text
2026-08-06 15:49:14.083 [error] InstantiationService has been disposed: Error: InstantiationService has been disposed
    at s._throwIfDisposed (.../sessions.desktop.main.js:1581:574)
    at s.createInstance (.../sessions.desktop.main.js:1581:1228)
    at gee._sendInlineCompletionsRequestTelemetry (.../sessions.desktop.main.js:983:26508)
    at .../sessions.desktop.main.js:983:23532
    at async RRe.trigger (.../sessions.desktop.main.js:983:51898)
```

Source-map resolution traced the failure to `InlineCompletionsSource._sendInlineCompletionsRequestTelemetry`. The request’s `finally` block sends end-of-life telemetry, but that method lazily created `DataChannelForwardingTelemetryService` through the editor-scoped `IInstantiationService`. If the editor was disposed while awaiting the provider, telemetry creation threw instead of completing cleanup.

## What changed

Create and retain the lightweight `DataChannelForwardingTelemetryService` when `InlineCompletionsSource` is constructed, while its DI scope is valid, and reuse it when asynchronous requests settle. This preserves the telemetry rather than adding a disposal guard that would silently drop it.

## Validation

- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/test/browser/inlineCompletions.test.ts` — 28 passing

title: Agent plugins: auto-update permanently fails with "Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches" due to concurrent git fetch/pull in the same plugin clone

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
- VS Code Version: Version: 1.132.0 (Universal), Commit: df53daabb18cd157bdb08c7f01c34df936cf12f4
- OS Version: macOS 26.3.1 (a) (25D771280a), Apple Silicon (also reported on Windows 11)
- Feature: Agent plugins (preview), plugin installed via `Chat: Install Plugin From Source`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the agent plugins preview.
2. Run `Chat: Install Plugin From Source` and enter a public git URL (repro repo: `https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-ai-toolkit`).
3. Let the upstream repo advance by at least one commit.
4. Restart VS Code. Having a second window (or the Sessions app) open makes it reproduce reliably.

## Expected

The cached plugin clone fast-forwards to the new upstream commit.

## Actual

An error notification appears on every launch:

> Failed to update: https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-ai-toolkit  [Show Output]

The plugin never updates again. The state is self-perpetuating: because the update never lands, the clone stays behind, so every subsequent launch has commits to fetch and fails the same way. Two independent users (macOS and Windows 11) report the plugin has never successfully updated since install.

`Show Output` opens the built-in Git extension's output channel, which contains nothing related to plugin updates, so the failure is undiagnosable from the UI.

## Logs

From `sharedprocess.log` (the only place the real error appears):

```
2026-08-06 13:09:52.018 [error] [LocalGitService] git fetch failed: Command failed: git fetch
error: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/main': is at cc5af6505c27939222072449278f6356857cb064 but expected 0e06bc35611e505e372de7f8cdf265e6d6dbc311
From https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-ai-toolkit
 ! 0e06bc3..cc5af65  main                -> origin/main  (unable to update local ref)
 * [new branch]      mirror/d8475f49b6ea -> origin/mirror/d8475f49b6ea

2026-08-06 13:09:52.101 [error] [LocalGitService] git fetch failed: Command failed: git fetch
error: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/main': is at cc5af6505c27939222072449278f6356857cb064 but expected 0e06bc35611e505e372de7f8cdf265e6d6dbc311
From https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-ai-toolkit
 ! 0e06bc3..cc5af65  main                -> origin/main  (unable to update local ref)
 * [new branch]      mirror/d8475f49b6ea -> origin/mirror/d8475f49b6ea

2026-08-06 13:09:52.912 [error] [LocalGitService] git pull failed: Command failed: git pull --ff-only
fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.
```

## Analysis

**1. Concurrent git operations in the same clone.** Two `git fetch` processes fail to lock `refs/remotes/origin/main` 83ms apart, both holding the pre-fetch value, which means a third fetch had already advanced the ref. So at least three `git fetch` processes were running in the same working directory at once.

`AgentPluginRepositoryService` serializes only *clones*:

```ts
private readonly _cloneSequencer = new SequencerByKey<string>();
...
return this._cloneSequencer.queue(repoDir.fsPath, async () => { ... });  // ensureRepository only
```

`pullRepository` and `fetchRepository` take no such lock, and `PluginInstallService.updateAll` fans its per-plugin git work out with `Promise.all(independentGitTasks)` (plus a separate `Promise.all(gitTasks)` for grouped ones). Several plugins/marketplaces backed by the same repository, an update check running alongside an update, or a second window / the Sessions app sharing the same `agent-plugins` directory all produce concurrent `git fetch`/`git pull` in one clone.

**2. Why it becomes a hard failure.** Each `git fetch` truncates and rewrites `FETCH_HEAD`. Concurrent fetches interleave, leaving more than one entry *not* marked `not-for-merge`. `git pull --ff-only` then reads that file and dies in `builtin/pull.c`:

```c
if (merge_heads.nr > 1) {
    if (opt_rebase)
        die(_("Cannot rebase onto multiple branches."));
    if (opt_ff && !strcmp(opt_ff, "--ff-only"))
        die(_("Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches."));
}
```

A single, uncontended fetch can never produce this. A manual sequential `git pull --ff-only` in the same clone succeeds immediately.

**3. The recovery path misses it.** `LocalGitService._isFastForwardPullFailure` requires exit code 128 *and* `/not possible to fast-forward|non-fast-forward/i`. `fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.` matches neither, so the error is rethrown before the fetch-and-retry and before the `allowHardResetOnDivergence` hard reset that would otherwise repair the clone.

**4. The failure is undiagnosable from the UI.** The notification drops the underlying error:

```ts
message: localize('updateAllFailed', "Failed to update: {0}", failedNames.join(', ')),
actions: {
    primary: [new Action('showGitOutput', localize('showOutput', "Show Output"), undefined, true, () => {
        this._commandService.executeCommand('git.showOutput');
    })],
}
```

`git.showOutput` opens the built-in Git extension's channel, but plugin updates run through `LocalGitService` in the shared process and never write there. Users see an empty/irrelevant log and have no way to reach the real error short of grepping `sharedprocess.log` for `LocalGitService`.

## Suggested fixes

1. Serialize git operations per repository directory, not just clones: reuse `SequencerByKey` keyed on `repoDir.fsPath` for `pullRepository`/`fetchRepository` as well. Because multiple windows and the Sessions app share the same clone, an on-disk lock is needed to fully close it, not just an in-process sequencer.
2. Avoid `FETCH_HEAD` entirely in `LocalGitService.pull`: `git fetch --prune` followed by `git merge --ff-only @{u}` is immune to this whole class of failure, since the merge head is named explicitly.
3. Treat `Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches` as a recoverable fast-forward failure in `_isFastForwardPullFailure`, so the existing retry/hard-reset recovery can repair the clone.
4. Include `err.message` in the `updateAllFailed` notification, and point its action at the log that actually contains the error rather than at `git.showOutput`.

## Workaround

Quit all VS Code windows (including the Sessions app), then run a single sequential pull in the cached clone:

```
git -C ~/.vscode/agent-plugins/<repo-dir> pull --ff-only
```

It fast-forwards cleanly. The error returns the next time upstream advances.

title: Distinguish rearmed voice approval occurrences
body:
## Summary

- assign each active tool approval or authentication prompt a stable occurrence ID derived from its request, tool call, pending phase, visible command, and authentication resource
- share that occurrence across rehydrated or presentation-only copies, while giving a re-armed or command-refreshed prompt a new timestamped token
- retire occurrences when the pending interaction ends so delayed voice responses cannot approve a later prompt
- keep authentication identity stable while the same request remains pending
- refresh the complete Agent Host prepared invocation when a pending command changes, and narrate the command actually shown to the user

## Root cause

The Agent Host can refresh, rehydrate, or re-arm a tool invocation while it is pending. Object and callback identity are not reliable occurrence boundaries: a callback can be recreated during a cosmetic refresh, retained across a meaningful command change, or represented by multiple invocation objects.

That made voice pending IDs either change while the same prompt was still active or remain unchanged when a genuinely new prompt replaced it. The former caused announcements and responses to miss; the latter allowed deduplication or a delayed spoken response to target the wrong occurrence.

## Implementation

Pending tool interactions now use a semantic key consisting of the request ID, tool-call ID, pending phase, normalized command, and authentication resource. An active-occurrence map assigns that key a timestamped token, tracks every invocation copy participating in it, and disposes the occurrence after those copies leave the pending state.

This keeps one prompt stable through presentation-only refreshes, gives a changed or re-armed prompt a fresh ID, and lets response dispatch reject stale IDs safely.

## Scope

This is the shared pending-occurrence fix extracted from #326698 so it can land independently. Omni-window session-routing behavior remains on that PR branch.

- ESLint on the changed files

title: Add voice session awareness and actions
body:
Part of #329488
Part of #329489
Part of #329490
Fixes #329491

## Summary

This adds the frontend foundation for session-aware Voice Mode:

- enriches the ongoing voice session context with session type, selected model, and attachment metadata
- expands `get_session_info` to include agent and regular chat sessions, aggregate state counts, target state, activity, and truncation metadata
- makes session focus/navigation retarget subsequent voice turns only after the requested surface is shown successfully
- adds frontend dispatch for voice-driven model selection and file attachment in workbench chat and the Agents/new-session composer
- strengthens the active listening indication against the actual themed input background with a 3:1 non-text contrast target

The branch is based directly on `main` and has no dependency on `megrogge/chat-input-window`.

## Frontend action contract

### Session context

Each `session_context.sessions[]` entry may now include:

- `session_type`: `agent` or `chat`
- `selected_model`: `{ identifier, name, vendor }`
- `attachment_names`: display names only; file contents remain frontend-owned until request submission
- `attachment_count`

`get_session_info` returns:

- `total_sessions`
- `counts`: `working`, `waiting_for_input`, and `idle`
- `sessions`: active target first, then most recently active, capped at 20
- `truncated`

The session list includes IDs, labels, types, state, active-target marker, activity age, response summary, model/attachment metadata, and agent change counts where available.

### Actions

- `focus_session({ coding_session_id })` reveals the session and makes it the target for later voice turns. It returns structured `ok`, `session_not_found`, or `switch_failed` results.
- `set_model({ model_id | model, coding_session_id? })` selects only an exact frontend identifier or unique normalized exact name. Ambiguous input returns candidates; the frontend does not guess.
- `attach_file` / `attach_files({ uri | path | uris | paths, coding_session_id? })` attach exact URIs or exact workspace-relative paths. With no file argument, the active editor is attached. Ambiguous workspace paths return candidates.
- Explicitly targeted model/attachment actions reveal and retarget the requested session before changing its input.

## Required voice-backend follow-up

No voice-backend code is available in this repository. The backend needs corresponding tool and routing changes before all user-facing flows are end to end:

1. Consume the added session context fields and use `get_session_info` for questions about the current session, session counts, running work, selected model, and attachments.
2. Register and emit `set_model` with `model_id` (preferred) or `model`, plus optional `coding_session_id`.
3. Register and emit `attach_file` / `attach_files` with `uri`, `path`, `uris`, or `paths`, plus optional `coding_session_id`. A call without file arguments means the active editor.
4. Treat `ambiguous_model` and `ambiguous_file` as clarification prompts. Do not claim that an action succeeded unless the frontend returned `ok: true`.
5. Treat "start a new session" as the existing `new_sessions` application action. Do not answer the utterance conversationally or submit it as prompt text to the current coding session.
6. After a successful `focus_session`, route subsequent turns to that returned session ID until the frontend target changes.

### Routing boundary

The voice backend should answer or act directly for application state/actions and lightweight questions that do not need workspace context or durable chat history. Examples include:

- "What session am I in?"
- "How many sessions are running?"
- "Is the agent still working?"
- "Which model am I using?"
- "Start a new session"
- "Change to GPT-5"
- "Attach this file"
- "What does polymorphism mean?"
- "While that request runs, what is the difference between TCP and UDP?"

It should submit a coding-agent chat request for work that requires workspace context, tools, repository inspection, project modification, or a durable answer in chat history. Examples include debugging a test, explaining a compiler error in the project, refactoring, searching the repository, reviewing a PR, creating a migration, or investigating a build.

Direct voice answers should not create a new coding request or pollute the active coding session while other work continues.

## Related fixes

#329441 and #329451 address the two previously reported persistence/playback bugs separately. Those changes look complementary to this work; this PR neither duplicates nor depends on them.

- targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files

title: tunnels: fail over to a dedicated agent host when the gateway rejects a selection
body:
A tunnel-backed connect could stay down for the whole reconnect backoff window instead of failing over to a dedicated agent host.

### The bug

The CLI's agent-host registry treats an entry as live purely by PID liveness, so an `editor` entry can outlive the socket it advertises. The gateway then answers the selection with `{"ok":false,"error":"Selected agent host became unreachable: ..."}` and closes:

```
debug Agent-host tunnel: dispatching /agent-host/select to protocol-v6 selection gateway
debug Gateway selection failed: Selected agent host became unreachable: Failed to connect to selected
      agent host socket at \\.\pipe\vscode-agent-host-<id>: could not connect to socket/pipe:
      Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "The system cannot find the file specified." }
```

`completeSelection` threw a plain `Error` for that, indistinguishable from the tunnel being unreachable, so `_connectTunnel` just rescheduled a reconnect — which resolved the identical stale `editor` endpoint from the still-unchanged inventory and failed the same way, over and over, until the owning PID finally died. The editor → standalone fallback and its notification did eventually fire, but only minutes later.

### The fix

Tag the gateway's `{"ok":false}` answer with a distinct `Error.name` (`TUNNEL_GATEWAY_SELECTION_REJECTED_ERROR_NAME`), carried as a name rather than an `Error` subclass because it crosses the shared-process IPC boundary, which preserves `name`/`message`/`stack` but not the prototype chain.

A rejection is the one failure that proves the tunnel is healthy and only the chosen endpoint is dead, so `_completeSelectionWithFallback` re-runs `prepareSelection` and retries once with `selectGatewayFallbackAfterRejection()` — a dedicated host, never the instance just rejected. The failover now happens inside a single connect attempt.

Every other failure means the tunnel itself is down and is rethrown unchanged, so the contribution keeps retrying the same destination and selection. A fallback never mutates the stored location preference, so the editor host is preferred again as soon as it is back.

### Notification

The substitution also notifies now, including on a user-initiated connect that explicitly asked for the editor host, since there is no earlier registration for the tracker to compare against within a single attempt. That case gets its own message, because nothing was reconnected or interrupted on a fresh connect.

A stale entry lingers for as long as its PID does and every later reconnect repeats the same fallback, so `shouldNotifyTunnelFailover` stays quiet once the address is already recorded as `standalone`.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, eslint on the touched files
- 78 passing unit tests across `gateway selection`, `TunnelAgentHost`, `PendingGatewaySelection`, and `gateway wire protocol`, including new coverage for the rejection tag, transport-failure classification, `selectGatewayFallbackAfterRejection`, and notification de-duplication

title: Fix Agents window tabs shifting vertically
body:
## Summary

- keep the Agents single-pane editor tabs independent from the shared compact editor-tab density
- add regression coverage for `window.density.editorTabHeight: compact`
- document the fixed tab-height contract in the single-pane layout

## Issue

After closing an integrated browser editor, the right-side **Changes / Files** tabs could intermittently render too high in the Agents window.

![Agents window Changes tab shifted against the top of its strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77630a20-d7a1-416c-ab3a-d37916759596)

## Analysis

Live inspection of the reproduced state showed the editor title had:

- the `compact-height` class
- an inline `--editor-group-tab-height: 22px`

The Agents tab strip owns different fixed geometry: 26px tab pills, 4px vertical padding, and the title divider, for a 35px title row. `SinglePaneMainEditorPart` already forced `showTabs: 'multiple'`, but still inherited the global `window.density.editorTabHeight` setting. That allowed the workbench tab control to calculate a compact 22px height while the Agents CSS continued rendering its fixed-size chrome.

The symptom was intermittent because editor-title lifecycle paths can either retain prior layout dimensions or recompute them from the compact option; closing a browser editor exposed the mismatched recomputation.

## Fix

Force `tabHeight: 'default'` together with `showTabs: 'multiple'` for the single-pane editor part. This keeps the JavaScript title reservation aligned with the Agents-owned tab geometry without changing shared editor behavior.

## Verification

- VS Code Version:    1.132.0 and 1.133.0-insider

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install a trusted Microsoft extension, such as [Docker](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-azuretools.vscode-docker)
2. Apply a configuration profile to allow _only_ Docker, [based on it's published attributes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-containers/blob/main/extensions/vscode-docker/package.json), using a payload like the following....

3. Relaunch VS Code and find that the Docker extension is disabled in spite of explicit approval.
4. Update the configuration profile to use a payload that references Microsoft's Trusted Publisher identity, like this...
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

        <key>AllowedExtensions</key>
        <string>{"microsoft": true}</string>
    </dict>
</plist>
```

- This does not appear to be a problem when using [private marketplace](https://github.com/microsoft/vsmarketplace/tree/main/privatemarketplace) because the client does not modify the Docker extension (or other Microsoft extensions) upon installation, like this...

title: mcp: add setting to exclude user-level MCP servers from a workspace
body:
## Summary

Adds `chat.mcp.userServersEnabled` (boolean, default `true`). When set to `false` in workspace settings, MCP servers configured at user or remote-user scope are excluded from resolution — only workspace-defined MCP servers (e.g. `.vscode/mcp.json`) remain available to the agent for that workspace.

This closes the gap described in #329475: VS Code already lets a workspace opt out of user-level configuration for agents (`chat.agentFilesLocations`), skills (`chat.agentSkillsLocations`), instructions (`chat.instructionsFilesLocations`), and hooks (`chat.hookFilesLocations`), but had no equivalent for MCP servers. Personal MCP configuration outside the workspace could still change what tools an agent has access to inside a project, which breaks reproducibility for teams that check in an MCP-based agent harness.

## Implementation notes

- The merge point for local MCP servers by scope is `McpWorkbenchService.getEnabledLocalMcpServers()` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/browser/mcpWorkbenchService.ts`), which is the single consumer feeding `InstalledMcpServersDiscovery`. Filtering there means the setting affects exactly what tools get registered/resolved, without touching how servers are listed/managed in the MCP Servers UI.
- `LocalMcpServerScope.User` and `LocalMcpServerScope.RemoteUser` are both excluded when the setting is `false`; `LocalMcpServerScope.Workspace` is always kept, so a workspace-defined server is never shadowed by an excluded user-scoped server of the same name.
- The setting is registered next to the existing `chat.mcp.access` toggle in `chat.shared.contribution.ts`, with no explicit `scope`, matching the sibling MCP settings (window-scope by default, settable in workspace settings).
- `chat.mcp.allowedServers` / `chat.mcp.deniedServers` were considered but don't fit: they're `ConfigurationScope.APPLICATION`-only, policy-delivered, hidden from the Settings UI, and match by server identity (name/URL/command) rather than scope — they can't express "keep workspace servers, drop everything from the user profile."

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck-client`
- [x] `npx eslint` on all changed files
- [x] Added unit tests in `mcpWorkbenchService.test.ts` covering: default (user servers included), exclusion when disabled (workspace servers kept), no shadowing of a workspace server by a same-named excluded user server, and re-evaluation on config change
- [x] Ran the full `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp` test suite (`./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/mcp/**/*.test.js"`) — 242 passing, no regressions

Opening this now to get the shape of the setting in front of the team for feedback — happy to adjust naming/scope/placement based on direction from whoever owns MCP settings.
